newsitem.title: USA: Estee Lauder results stronger across the board.
newsitem.headline: Estee Lauder results stronger across the board.

text.p: The Estee Lauder Cos. Inc., the cosmetics and fragrances company, Tuesday reported higher earnings for the fourth quarter and full fiscal year, citing strong sales in all of its brands.

"The significant sales performance by all of our brands, as well as the success of our initiatives to enhance operating margins resulted in an excellent performance for our company," said Leonard A. Lauder, chairman.
"Going forward our goal is to continue to produce solid growth and increase stockholder value."
Earnings for the fourth quarter rose to $36.7 million, or 26 cents a share, from $27.3 million, or 18 cents a share, in the year-earlier period.
Sales for the fourth quarter rose to $775.9 million from $736.7 million.

For the year ended June 30, sales rose 6 percent to $3.4 billion from $3.2 billion in the prior year. Excluding the impact of foreign currency translation, net sales increased 9 percent during the year.
Earnings rose to $197.6 million, or $1.46 a share, from $102.9 million. Comparable per-share figures were not available, as the company went public in November, 1995.

Estee Lauder said sales of makeup products rose 11 percent during the year to $1.3 billion due to new products in the Clinique, Prescriptives and Estee Lauder lines, the ongoing strength of existing products and higher sales from MAC and Bobbi Brown essentials.

Sales in the fragrance category grew 6 percent over the prior year to $822.7 million led by strong worldwide sales of "tommy" and the success of "tommy girl" in the United States as well as higher sales of the Estee Lauder signature fragrance and White Linen Breeze.
Estee Lauder stock was up $1.8125 to $48.8125 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
